text:
eva: nightly-eval alert: 3 suites failed for model=rw-instruct-7b-quant4cohort variant. failing suites: instruct-qa, code-gen-short, summarization-short. alert severity: medium. link: https://internal.evals/runs/1954320
alice: on it — first pass: could be a false positive from nouveau tokenization change?
ben: which commit rolled this variant in?
eva: rolled yesterday at 02:14 UTC, commit `deploy/quant-cohort-2026-03-18`
carla: quick grep of failures looks like hallucinated citations in instruct-qa prompts (legal-qa-001) and truncated outputs for summarization-short
ben: can you paste a failing example?
carla: ```
input: "Summarize the following paragraph..."
output (quant4): "In summary, the study found that the data proves that X was responsible. [see ref]"
baseline (fp16): "In summary, the study found several factors likely contributing to X; see Table 2 for details."
```
dan: weird — the quant4 outputs look more assertive and shorter. maybe decoding temperature or EOS handling regressed
oncall-ml: @alice you're oncall for eng-ml today per rota
alice: ack, taking ownership. immediate plan: 1) rerun failing suites against fp16 baseline + quant4 variant on same hardware; 2) run diffscript to count tokenization deltas; 3) check KV-cache boundary logs for truncated gens
ci-bot: rerun jobs queued: eval/instruct-qa/1954321000 (queued), eval/summarization-short/1954321001 (queued), eval/code-gen-short/1954321002 (queued)
ben: add me as backup. I'll look into tokenization diff tooling (tok-diff)
alice: ok ran tok-diff on a sample: 12/200 prompt pairs had different tokenization; most are punctuation-related. not enough to explain 3x failure rate
carla: I dumped model logits for a failing prompt — quant4 shows spiking around end-of-sequence token earlier than fp16. attaching excerpt: `logits[t-1]` skewed +3.2 std dev
dan: could be kernel selection: runtime chose `attn-opt-v2` for quant path; fallback in fp16 used `attn-opt-v1`. @eng-runtime to confirm kernel mapping?
oncall-ml: pinging eng-runtime channel for `attn-opt-v2` rollout status
eva: immediate severity: set to P2 (customer-impacting for a small cohort). owner: alice, backup: ben. ETA for initial findings: 2h
alice: reruns finished: instruct-qa still failing on quant4 (fail rate 18% vs baseline 1.2%), summarization-short fail 11% vs 0.5%, code-gen-short marginal but above threshold (4% vs 0.3%)
ben: tokenization not root cause. looking at logits and head pruning interactions now
carla: trying a hotfix test: run quant4 with `decode_timeout=1200` and `eos_penalty=0` to see if truncation reduces failures
dan: also try forcing kernel `attn-opt-v1` on quant4 variant to replicate fp16 path
ci-bot: hotfix test queued: eval/instruct-qa/hotfix-1954321003
alice: timeline update: will have kernel-forcing test in ~45m. if kernel swap reproduces baseline, plan: patch runtime to prefer v1 for quant4 until we root cause
eva: customer impact note: queued jobs from a few private tenants might have seen bad outputs. CS notified with high-level note, no public incident yet
alice: documenting in runbook: https://go/runbooks/eval-regressions -> adding steps and links to logs
ben: if kernel choice is culprit, we should also run quant4 on a different GPU type (A10 vs A100) to rule out hardware-specific numerics
carla: agreed. I'll queue cross-GPU run after kernel test
dan: good triage. capture a reproducible minimal prompt and add to failing promptset so we can add a canary check in nightly
oncall-ml: moving channel to follow-up thread when we have root cause. Good work team :thumbsup:
eva: thanks — keep updates here for next 2h. if severity escalates to P1, I'll page SRE and comms.
